title: VPC endpoint policy reconciler Terraform module and upgrade-safe route reconciler
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that centralizes creation and reconciliation of VPC Endpoints (Interface and Gateway), endpoint policies, and associated route table entries across Redwood private deployments. The module must be upgrade-safe: it should permit staged updates without causing transient routing blackholes, reconcile drift between configuration and actual AWS state, and provide health checks + CloudWatch alarms for endpoint reachability. This aims to reduce manual post-deploy fixes, simplify cross-account endpoint sharing patterns, and make endpoint policy changes auditable and reversible.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables for endpoint definitions (service name, type, subnet ids, security groups, custom policy JSON) and outputs created endpoint IDs and ENI IPs

Running terraform plan/apply on an existing deployment with changed endpoint policy performs a staged update: creates any new endpoints, updates policies with no downtime, then deletes old resources only after new endpoints report healthy status
Automated route reconciliation ensures route tables referencing gateway endpoints are updated atomically during upgrades (no 5+ minute route blackholes observed in a canary run)
Module emits CloudWatch metrics and creates sample alarms for EndpointHealthy (synthetic TCP/HTTP probe) and EndpointPolicyDrift detected
Module supports cross-account endpoint sharing via AWS RAM by optional enablement flag and documents IAM/RAM prerequisites
Comprehensive unit-level examples in README: single-account private deployment, multi-account shared services, and air-gapped on-prem variant (no RAM)
Integration test run against a sandbox account demonstrates zero-traffic-loss during a policy change with canary=false and controlled rollout when canary=true
tasks: Design API surface: inputs, outputs, and policy templating placeholders
Implement core Terraform resources for aws_vpc_endpoint (interface/gateway), aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association, and optional aws_ram_resource_share
Add null_resource + local-exec reconciliation hook for listing current endpoints/route associations to detect drift
Implement health-check Lambda or synthetic probe using AWS Synthetics/CloudWatch Synthetics and expose metrics EndpointHealthy
Create example usages (single-account, shared-services multi-account) and CI integration test in infra-integration pipeline
Document upgrade & rollback procedures in README and infra runbook
Security review: validate endpoint policy templating to avoid privilege escalation (least-privilege templates + validator)
implementation_notes: Prefer pure Terraform 1.6+ constructs and avoid provider-specific external scripting where possible. For drift detection and atomic reconciliation, we will add an optional null_resource with a small Go-based helper run via local-exec in CI/CD to compute required route changes and emit plan warnings. Where AWS primitives cannot guarantee zero-downtime (e.g., changing gateway endpoint service names), the module will provide a "staged_rollout" flag to create replacement endpoints and update route tables during a maintenance window. Endpoint policy templating will accept either raw JSON strings or a path to template files; policy validation will use aws_iam_policy_document data source and a lightweight JSON schema check in CI. Cross-account sharing via RAM will be optional and gated behind an explicit enable flag and documented prerequisites (org permissions + resource share roles).
variables_reference: vpc_id - id of VPC to attach endpoints to
subnet_ids - list of subnet ids for interface endpoints
route_table_ids - list of route table ids for gateway endpoints
endpoints - list of maps: {name, service, type (interface|gateway), policy_json, security_group_ids, private_dns_enabled, enable_ram_share}
staged_rollout - bool (default false) to enable replacement-first updates
healthcheck_config - optional map: {probe_port, probe_path, frequency_seconds, failure_threshold}
outputs_reference: endpoint_ids - list of created endpoint ids
endpoint_private_ips - list of ENI private IPs for interface endpoints
route_associations - list of route table -> endpoint associations
policy_change_plan - textual summary emitted during plan when policy drift detected
rollout_plan: Merge module code and examples behind feature flag in infra library branch
Run CI integration tests in sandbox account with staged_rollout=false - verify basic create/update/delete
Run canary with staged_rollout=true on a non-critical VPC and validate health metrics for 24h
Open a small internal RFC + runbook and get signoff from SRE and Security
Deploy to production following maintenance window if staged_rollout=true, otherwise live deploy with monitoring enabled
If policy-change causes unexpected failures, rollback by reapplying last-known-good variables and triggering route reconciliation helper
monitoring: CloudWatch metric: EndpointHealthy (1/0) emitted from Synthetics or Lambda probe
CloudWatch alarm: EndpointHealthy < 1 for 3 consecutive probes -> alert to platform-oncall
CloudWatch metric: EndpointPolicyDriftDetected (increment on mismatch between desired and observed policy) -> routed to infra team channel
Dashboard: per-VPC endpoint latency, interface ENI error counts, and route table change history (from CloudTrail)
test_plan: Unit: tf validate and example module plan diff checks in CI
Integration: apply module in sandbox account and run synthetic probes against interface endpoints
Chaos test: create concurrent route changes and assert no packet loss in canary VPC for 30 minutes
Upgrade test: change policy JSON in a controlled run and assert staged_rollout avoids route blackholes
security_considerations: Endpoint policies are sensitive; enforce least-privilege templates and forbid wildcard principals in default templates
Enable logging for AWS PrivateLink endpoints where supported and route logs to secure S3 bucket with lifecycle policies
RAM sharing requires cross-account consent; document required roles and restrict to known AWS account IDs via allowlist
All module code changes must pass a security review before release (security_review_required=true)
